      static void player_capture_fires_filled_bucket_criterion_but_automation_does_not(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)

    • release_replaces_uuid_that_is_already_in_use

      static void release_replaces_uuid_that_is_already_in_use(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      No in-game form: a player cannot copy a stored mob while its original is still in the world. Guards that releasing a snapshot whose UUID is already in use gives the released mob a new UUID and leaves the existing mob alone.

    • released_non_bucketable_mob_does_not_despawn

      static void released_non_bucketable_mob_does_not_despawn(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A released mob that has no mob bucket of its own is made persistent, as vanilla does for a bucketed fish. In game: capture a naturally spawned zombie, release it, walk more than 128 blocks away and back: it is still there.

    • oversized_mob_is_not_captured

      static void oversized_mob_is_not_captured(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A mob whose saved data is too large for clients to receive in an item is not captured; the fixture weighs a pig down with one heavy held item in place of a loaded inventory. In game: load a chested donkey with stacks of long written books and try to bucket it: the action bar says it carries too much and the donkey stays.
